title: Deferred-execution reservoir and tokenized backlog playbook for cross-region load shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: During region outages and sudden traffic spikes we need a graceful way to preserve high-value requests while avoiding hard failures for best-effort workloads. Existing mechanisms (priority lanes + probabilistic shedding) aggressively drop work and do not allow short-lived deferred completion. Proposal: introduce a 'deferred-execution reservoir' (DER) that transiently accepts lower-priority requests for time-bound deferred processing, coupled with per-tenant 'tokenized backlog credits' (TBCs) that govern how much deferred work each tenant can accrue. The DER is a slow-path executor with configurable retention (default 15s) and a bounded execution rate; requests in DER may be completed at reduced fidelity (smaller output length, quantized model variant, or cached-response substitution) depending on the configured graceful-degradation mode. The system will integrate with cross-region circuit-bridge signals so that when a primary region fails, a sink region can import TBCs for affected tenants to continue deferred processing with controlled risk. Goals: 1) reduce hard failures for best-effort tiers, 2) preserve P99 and P50 for high-priority lanes by moving non-critical load into DER, 3) allow operators to reason about backlog liability via token accounting and dashboards. This ticket captures design, trade-offs, instrumentation, rollout, and runbook for DER+TBC.
acceptance_criteria: DER accepts and time-bounds deferred requests and either completes them or expires with a documented failure path
Per-tenant TBC accounting emits Prometheus metrics: tbc_accrued, tbc_spent, tbc_imported, tbc_exported
High-priority lanes maintain existing SLOs (p99 latency degradation < 5%) under simulated 3x baseline burst when DER is enabled
Cross-region circuit-bridge can transfer up to configured fraction of TBCs during failover and transfer events are visible in Grafana
Canary rollout with feature flag shows no increase in error budget burn for production customers in first 72h
design_decisions: Use a bounded time-window (config default 15s) for DER retention rather than unbounded backlog to limit liability
Tokenized backlog credits are consumed on enqueue and can be imported/exported across regions via the circuit-bridge protocol
DER processing is a slow-path pool using a quantized model variant by default (e.g., int8) to control cost
Requests in DER are tagged with a degradation policy (length cap, n-best pruning, function-call veto) that can be overridden per-tenant
Admission into DER is scored by composite key: tenant_priority, request_cost_estimate, recent_failure_rate, and tbc_balance
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces hard drops and preserves user-perceived availability for best-effort workloads; operators gain visibility into backlog liability
Cons: DER adds complexity (new accounting surface, cross-region token sync) and increases tail latency for deferred workloads; risk of backlog accumulation if retention/configs mis-set
We accept potential increased cost for slow-path executions to protect high-priority SLOs; mitigation via quantized models and strict time-bounds
Per-tenant TBCs require storage and atomicity guarantees; we choose optimistic updates with reconciliation to avoid global serialization at scale
rollout_plan: 1) Implement DER prototype behind feature flag in staging; run synthetic burst tests against existing priority lanes
2) Add TBC metrics and basic dashboard (tbc_accrued / spent / imported / exported) and alert on negative balances or import failures
3) Canary deploy to 5% of traffic in low-risk region, monitor p50/p95/p99, error budget burn, and DER expiration rate
4) Enable cross-region import for a subset of tenants with manual failover during scheduled maintenance
5) Gradually increase canary to 50% while enabling automated circuit-bridge transfers with throttles
6) Full rollout with playbook and automated rollback if p99 increases by >5% or DER expiration rate >2% after 24h
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: DER_expiration_rate > 1% sustained for 10m => create incident (SEV3)
Alert: p99 latency for priority lanes increases >5% above baseline for 5m => rollback canary flag
